transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Um... I don't know, I guess I'm just... really drained. My body feels completely drained. Like... even just walking from my car into the clinic today took everything I have. Work is... I don't know. Just opening the EHR takes all my energy. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Have you noticed that you don't enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you've lost interest in activities you normally like doing?
Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't... I haven't really paid attention to that, I guess. I just don't do much right now anyway.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, lately?

Yeah... I guess so. Just... empty, mostly. After all that energy I had just dropped, I started feeling pretty hopeless. Like... like I've already ruined my future in healthcare, and it hasn't even really started yet. So... yeah, most days are like that.
Have you found that you don’t take pleasure in things anymore or that you’ve lost interest in activities you used to enjoy?
Um... I think you just asked me that. But, um... I still don't really know. I just don't have the energy to do anything right now anyway, so... I haven't really noticed.
Have you been feeling like you're not good enough or that you've let others down, even if it's not necessarily your fault?

Um... yeah, I guess. I just... I keep thinking about work. Like, replaying every chart and... every set of vitals in my head. I just get this feeling that I... that I hurt the patients somehow. Even though my supervisors keep telling me nothing bad happened. It just... it feels like I did.
Can you think of any activity, even small ones, that you still enjoy or look forward to doing?
I don't know. Not really. I just... I don't really look forward to anything right now. I just want to sleep.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or that your thoughts feel slowed down? Or on the flip side, have you felt restless or fidgety lately?

Um... yeah. People at work... they told me I looked slowed down. And... I guess I felt it, too. Like... just putting a blood pressure cuff away, or... or trying to answer a simple question... it just took me way longer than it should have.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately? Like eating much less than usual or losing weight without trying?

Um... yeah. I guess I haven't really been eating much. I'd just... skip lunch and dinner mostly. I didn't really want food. Just drank coffee or water. I did notice my scrubs were fitting a lot looser... hanging off me, kind of.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um... maybe nine months? I guess. Just... feeling exhausted and... guilty all the time. It started when I crashed. I had this... really high-energy period before that, and then... I just crashed. It's been like this since then.
Have you had periods like this before, where you felt this way for several months at a time?
Um... no. I don't think so. Just... just this time, really.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely energetic, unusually confident, or so restless that you couldn't slow down, even if it felt good at the time?

Um... yeah, I guess. Before the crash. Some days I just... felt amazing. Like I was unstoppable. But... I don't know. If someone at work corrected my documentation, or... told me to slow down, I'd get mad. I'd kind of snap at them. It just... it felt like they were insulting me. That's all.
Can you tell me more about that high-energy period before the crash? How long did it last, and how was it different from your usual self?

Um... I don't know. It was... maybe two months? The whole thing kind of built up over that time. It started after they... they changed my responsibilities at the clinic. I just... I guess I was different then.
During that high-energy period before the crash, did you ever feel like you didn’t need much sleep, were more talkative than usual, or felt your thoughts were racing faster than normal?

Um... yeah. Sleep was... different. Before, I mean. I'd maybe get two, three hours... and I'd still be completely wired the next day. Like I didn't need it. But... it's not like that now. Lately, I just... I wake up really early, before the sun, just sick to my stomach with everything. Or... or I sleep until noon and I'm still just... so tired.
During that high-energy period before the crash, did you ever feel like you had so much energy that you didn’t need much sleep, or that your thoughts were racing so fast you couldn’t keep up?

Um... yeah, I guess. I just... I couldn't really sit still. At the clinic, I'd just keep walking the halls. I'd reorganize the supply closets, check the rooms... I just kept looking for more things to do. Even when my shift was supposed to be over, I just... kept going. I didn't want to stop.

During that high-energy period before the crash, did you ever feel like your mood was unusually elevated or irritable most of the time, or that you were doing things that were out of character for you, like taking on too many tasks or acting impulsively?

Um... I guess my mood was just... up and down. Some days I felt... I don't know, amazing. Like I was unstoppable. But then... if one of the nurses corrected my documentation, or... told me to slow down... I'd just snap. Like they were insulting me or something. I didn't mean to, it just... happened.

Before the crash, did you ever feel like your mood was extremely high or euphoric, or that you were doing things that were out of character for you, like taking on too many tasks or acting impulsively, even if it felt good at the time?

Um... I guess so. I was just... doing a lot. I started making all these new workflow plans for the floor... messaging my coworkers after hours about them. I even, um... I offered to train some people. Which was stupid, because I was barely ahead of them. I just kept taking on extra tasks... until I, um... I couldn't even finish my basic ones safely. So... yeah.
Have you ever had a period where you felt so unusually high, irritable, or full of energy that it was clearly different from your usual self, even if it felt good at the time?

I mean... I think I already said this, but yeah. It was... different. Sometimes I felt really good, like I was just... unstoppable. But then... if someone told me I was doing something wrong, or... told me to slow down... I'd just get really mad. I'd snap at them. It felt like they were... I don't know, attacking me. So... yeah, it was different.
